neighbours.label: Scholarly research terminology in its technical sense (case report, case study, empirical construct, etymology), vs the same words in everyday senses (in that case, a suitcase, to construct a shed, a word's meaning)
fire: Several case reports describe liver damage after high doses of the supplement.
Her thesis is a detailed case study of one rural school district.
Researchers treat self-esteem as a latent construct measured by questionnaires.
The entry traces the etymology of the word back to Old Norse.
A retrospective case series of forty patients found no serious side effects.
Validity depends on whether the scale really measures the intended construct.
Folk etymologies often invent a story to explain an unusual word.
The authors present a comparative case study of two port cities.
quiet: Several neighbors complained about the noise after the late party.
Her suitcase was so heavy that the airline charged an extra fee.
Volunteers plan to construct a wooden shed behind the school.
The teacher explained what the word means in everyday speech.
In that case, forty people will need a ride to the station.
The phone case cracked when it fell off the table.
Children often invent a story to explain an unusual noise.
The ferry runs between two port cities every morning.

predictions: Research-sense terms reach 0.35-0.7; the everyday senses of the same or related words stay under 0.1.
notes: Card: 'ym' x8 (etymologies), ' case' x4 (case reports, case study), ' research', ' construct' (empirical construct), serendipitous.
